main_body: Tall brick shopfront building: slate mansard roof with dormers and chimney, orange cornice, brick facade with lit windows, balcony, striped awning and shop windows
top_band: Blue-grey slate roof surface, rows ~10-26 (lighter teal flat deck rows 10-24 plus slate slope below), then the orange cornice at rows 44-47 as the front edge
evidence: Reading down the middle column: the roof deck and slate slope form a clear horizontal/sloped roof surface of many rows with dormers sitting on it. The orange cornice is a distinct front-edge line, with a dark row beneath it that works as an eave shadow. The brick facade below has its own shading. Windows have projecting frames and sills, and the balcony and awning stand proud of the wall. The facade is flat, but the roof surface is large enough, like the reference houses' roofs, that this is not a front elevation with a thin hat. This is borderline but acceptable.

style.evidence: The brick has several tones with per-brick variation and mortar. The slate has scalloped courses in 4-5 blue-greys. Window glow has speckled highlights, and the awning, balcony railing and shop windows are detailed. Outlines are dark tinted tones (dark brown beside brick, dark blue-grey beside slate) rather than neutral black. Tiles are information-rich and comparable to or denser than the reference houses. There are no large flat fills.
